newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK journalists welcome China paroling reporter.
newsitem.headline: HK journalists welcome China paroling reporter.

text.p: The Hong Kong Journalists Association welcomed China's decision to release on parole on Saturday Hong Kong newspaper reporter Xi Yang three years into his prison sentence for stealing state secrets.
"At the eve of handover of Hong Kong sovereignty, we appreciate that the Beijing authority has sent a positive signal to Hong Kong," the association said in a statement on Sunday.
"We always believed Xi Yang was doing his job as a professional journalist and his imprisonment was unwarranted."
China jailed Xi, now 40, for 12 years in March 1994 on charges of stealing state secrets about internal policies on interest rates and gold.
The severity of the sentence shocked Hong Kong reporters, already pessimistic about the prospects for a free press after the handover and triggered protests in the British colony.
"The return of Xi Yang is the result of concerted efforts of media professionals and the public at large in campaigning for his release," the association added.
"We hope that the Beijing government would have more understanding and flexibility in responding to Hong Kong journalists covering news in mainland China."
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, 1997.
